data.content:
The Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Communication & Works Department is seeking a contractor who can rehabilitate, widen and improve 64 km of district roads under Package‑IV, while also reconstructing three reinforced concrete bridges (40 m, 65 m and 110 m) and delivering associated drainage, retaining structures and road safety furniture within a 24‑month construction period that spans two monsoon seasons.

We understand that success for C&W will be measured by: (i) keeping the corridor safely serviceable for local traffic during works through disciplined traffic management and sequencing, (ii) achieving durable pavement performance through controlled earthworks and layer construction supported by fit‑for‑purpose QA/QC and testing, (iii) completing bridge and structure works to design intent with strict control of concrete quality and curing during wet seasons, and (iv) minimizing environmental and community impacts, particularly where the works interact with drainage lines, slopes and any protected watershed constraints.

Our methodology will therefore be built around a CPM-based work program that explicitly models monsoon constraints and protects critical path activities (earthworks, pavement layers, bridge substructure/superstructure and approach tie-ins). We will also align delivery with a documented HSE policy and our recorded zero reportable fatalities, supported by site safety plans on infrastructure deployments [CO-PROFILE].

We also recognize key compliance expectations in the bid process (single stage one envelope submission and bid security PKR 37 million). We can arrange CDR/bank guarantee up to our facility limit [CO-PROFILE].

Where the RFP requires evidence beyond our current library, we will address it transparently: our records do not evidence PEC constructor registration in C‑A/C‑1, ISO 14001 certification, three road contracts ≥ PKR 700 million, or average annual turnover ≥ PKR 1,500 million [CO-PROFILE]; and our bridge project records do not state span ≥ 60 m (though we have delivered bridge engineering deployments including a PKR 200M engagement) [CAP-028]. We will close these gaps via compliant partnering and pre-award mobilization of qualified resources.
